tagline.text: A cave chapel where light pours through a hole in the ceiling

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱800–2,000 per person (half day from Tuguegarao)

children.text: A limestone cave in Peñablanca near Tuguegarao, where a chapel is set up in the first chamber beneath a shaft of sunlight streaming through a hole in the ceiling. It's also where fossils of the new hominin species Homo luzonensis were found, and the sight of bats swarming over the river at dusk is well known too.
Callao Cave is a limestone cave in Peñablanca, about
24km

northeast of Tuguegarao, the capital of Cagayan province. It sits within the Peñablanca Protected Landscape on the western foothills of the Sierra Madre range, an area said to hold around 300 caves large and small. Callao Cave is the most famous and most accessible of them, and a signature stop on any trip through the Cagayan Valley.

The cave opens partway up a hill overlooking the Pinacanauan River, reached by climbing about 184 concrete steps to the entrance. Inside, seven chambers connect one after another; the first is a vast space about
wide and
high. Sunlight slants in through a hole in the ceiling, and below it a small chapel has been set up using a rock as an altar, giving the space the feel of a cathedral built by nature itself.
This cave is also important in human history. In
an excavation team led by the Filipino archaeologist Armand Mijares found a human foot bone in the cave, and as more teeth and bones turned up, it was announced in

in the scientific journal Nature as a new archaic human, Homo luzonensis. At the time of the announcement the fossils were estimated to be at least 50,000 to 67,000 years old, but uranium-series dating in
pushed that back to about 134,000 years ago. They are the oldest human fossils found in the Philippines.
Callao Cave was designated one of the Philippines' earliest national parks in

. Inside, lighting and a walkway make it easy for anyone to explore without special gear, and adding the bat cave across the river and an evening river cruise fills out a satisfying half day. It's recommended for families, anyone who wants to combine history with nature, and travelers planning a trip through northern Cagayan.

blocks.title: The cave chapel bathed in light

children.text: The sight of sunlight pouring through the ceiling hole into the first chamber is Callao Cave's signature image. Mass and even weddings are still sometimes held at the chapel, which has wooden pews and a rock altar. The shaft of light is sharpest around midday, when the sun is highest.
Each chamber has its own mix of ceiling holes, stalactites, stalagmites, and flowstone. Guides point out rock formations that resemble an elephant's head or a praying figure, one by one.

You can see the excavation site and information panels where the new hominin fossils were found. The fossils themselves are studied and kept at institutions like the National Museum in Manila, so a visit to the National Museum's anthropology wing before or after your trip helps complete the story.

A small boat can carry you across or upriver along the green Pinacanauan River flowing beneath the cave entrance, offering views of the limestone cliffs. Some routes include a stop to rest on a sandbar along the bank.

blocks.title: Sunset flight of the bat colony

children.text: Around sunset (usually

), hundreds of thousands of bats are said to stream out of the riverside bat cave in a long line, forming a dark band across the sky. Watching from a boat on the river is the most striking way to see it.

Sierra Cave, within Callao Cave's tourism zone, is a "living cave" where stalactites are still growing today. It includes a section where you crawl through a narrow gap, making it a good match for adventurous travelers, and a guide is required.

Climbing to the viewpoint on the hill around the cave gives you a sweeping view of the winding Pinacanauan River and the Sierra Madre range. A small admission fee is all it takes to climb up without a guide.

If you want to see the ceiling's shaft of light at its best, it also works well to see the cave first in the morning, relax at a riverside resort, and watch the bat colony at dusk as a full-day plan. The cave generally stops admitting visitors around 4:30 PM, so arrive in good time.

This route avoids the midday heat and is good for seeing the beams of light. The day after heavy rain, first check the river level and whether the cave is open through a tricycle driver or your accommodation.
Philippine Airlines and Cebu Pacific fly from Manila to Tuguegarao Airport (TUG) in about
1 hour–1 hour 10 minutes
. The airport is close to town, so you can head straight there by tricycle.
Tuguegarao-bound buses such as Victory Liner and Florida run daily from Cubao, Pasay, and Sampaloc in Manila. The distance is about
480km
, it takes about
11–13 hours
, and the fare is about
depending on seat class. An overnight bus arrives in the morning.
Chartering a tricycle from Tuguegarao town to Callao Cave takes about
40 minutes–1 hour
. Negotiate around
one way, or around
for a round trip with waiting time. If you're also going to see the bats, agree on the wait time in advance.
To save money, take a jeepney from Tuguegarao town toward Peñablanca (about
), then switch to a tricycle in town to reach the cave entrance (about
). Return trips become scarce quickly around sunset.
If you're in a larger group, renting a van with a driver in Tuguegarao is more convenient, at about
for a half day.
The Cagayan Valley is one of the hottest regions in the Philippines.
December–February
is relatively cool with little rain, the best time for climbing the stairs and a river cruise.
March–May
is also dry with clear skies, but midday temperatures in Tuguegarao can climb to
. During this period, spend the midday hours inside the cool cave and move around in the early morning or late afternoon.
June–November
is the rainy season, and typhoons moving up into northeastern Luzon pass through Cagayan often, especially in
August–November

. Heavy rain can raise the Pinacanauan River's level, halting boat trips and sometimes temporarily closing the cave's tourism zone. Holy Week and long holidays draw crowds of local visitors, so it's best to arrive early in the morning.

It's convenient to base yourself in Tuguegarao town, where transport and restaurants are concentrated, with plenty of business hotels and pensions at about

a night. If you'd rather relax quietly in nature, cottages and simple rooms are available around the Callao Cave Resort area on the riverbank below the cave, though facilities there are basic, so keep your expectations modest.

If you're in Tuguegarao, be sure to try pancit Batil Patung, the region's signature noodle dish — thick noodles topped with carabao (water buffalo) meat and liver, a poached egg, and served with a side of egg soup, chopped onion, calamansi, and soy sauce. It's easy to find at pancitierias (noodle shops) around town. Chicharabao, fried carabao skin, and Cagayan-style longganisa are other local specialties, while stalls around the cave entrance sell only simple drinks and snacks.
The ceiling's shaft of light is sharpest around
10 AM–2 PM
, when the sun is high, while the bats emerge at dusk. To catch both, arrive early in the afternoon and see the cave first.
With around 184 steps, the climb isn't too strenuous, but you'll work up a sweat on a hot day. Bring water and climb at an easy pace.
The cave floor is dirt and rock, which can be slippery. Wear sneakers rather than sandals.
Local guides explain the rock formations and history. If there's no fixed rate, confirm the fee or tip level before you start.

When you register at the entrance visitor center and buy a ticket, you are lent a helmet, and one local guide accompanies each group of about 4 people. The guide fee has a minimum set by the Peñablanca Protected Landscape and Seascape management board, so check the amount before you start.
The chapel is still used as an active place of worship. If Mass or a wedding is underway, watch quietly from the back.
Book a bat-watching boat at the riverbank in the afternoon to make sure you can get one at dusk.
If you're planning to see the bats and return by tricycle, be sure to arrange your ride back after dark in advance. Vehicles are hard to find at night in Peñablanca.
Making this your first stop on a loop through northern Cagayan toward Palaui Island or Pagudpud is an efficient way to plan your route.

After a typhoon or heavy rain, the river level can rise enough to suspend boat trips and cave visits. Cagayan sees frequent typhoons, so check the weather and local notices before setting out during the rainy season.
Stalactites and stalagmites stop growing if even the oil from your hands touches them. Don't touch or remove anything from the cave walls or rock formations.
Don't use flash photography or shout at the bats. It's a good idea to cover your mouth and nose near bat droppings.
Narrow passages like Sierra Cave should only be entered with a guide, and anyone with claustrophobia shouldn't push themselves.
Heatstroke risk is high at midday during the dry season. Bring a hat and water, and rest often in the shade.
Wear a life vest on the boat, and don't board any boat that's over its passenger limit.
After heavy rain in
July 2025
, rocks fell from the cave ceiling twice, and the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) temporarily closed the cave in
August
. It may close again after heavy rain, so check whether it is operating before you set out, and be sure to wear a helmet inside the cave.
